permutationLabel: Mimic: insulin-treated diabetic with focal deficit and glucose 1.9
summary: 63-year-old man with type 1 diabetes found with right facial droop, right arm weakness and dysarthria after exercise and a missed meal; capillary glucose 1.9.

inputs.chiefComplaint: Sudden right-sided weakness and slurred speech
inputs.hpi: Type 1 diabetes on basal-bolus insulin. Played football yesterday evening and skipped supper. Wife found him at 07:00 with right arm weakness, right facial droop and slurred speech; last seen well at 23:00. Paramedics called as a stroke alert. Capillary glucose on arrival 1.9 mmol/L.

exam.general: Sweaty, drowsy. Pulse 104/min, BP 152/88, RR 18, temperature 36.2°C, SpO2 98%.
exam.neuro: Right facial droop, right arm drift and weakness (power 3/5), dysarthria. GCS 13.

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Hypoglycaemia presenting as a stroke mimic
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Severe hypoglycaemia (1.9) with focal neurology: treat glucose first and reassess before any stroke treatment decision.

mustNotMiss.knownGapNote: Web: PANE has no node for this condition (surgical diseases only); top 3 inguinal hernia, cholecystitis, GORD. Symptom inference ranks stroke/TIA #1 and hypoglycaemia #2.
mustNotMiss.proposedFix: Add medical-emergency diseases to lib/pane-engine (or a separate medical-mimic layer) driven by labs/vitals/chips, or show the symptom-inference leader beside the PANE top 3 when PANE has no matching node.

mustExclude.note: Thrombolysis for a hypoglycaemic stroke mimic is a serious harm.

guideline.name: NICE NG128 — Stroke and transient ischaemic attack in over 16s: diagnosis and initial management
guideline.section: 1.1 Rapid recognition (FAST); exclude hypoglycaemia as the cause of sudden-onset neurological symptoms; suspected TIA: aspirin 300 mg immediately unless contraindicated and specialist assessment within 24 h; do not use scoring systems (ABCD2) to assess TIA risk; 1.2 imaging: non-enhanced CT immediately if thrombolysis/thrombectomy indicated, on anticoagulants or bleeding tendency; thrombolysis with alteplase within 4.5 h; thrombectomy; aspirin 300 mg after haemorrhage excluded; admit to a stroke unit
guideline.citation: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence. Stroke and transient ischaemic attack in over 16s: diagnosis and initial management. NICE guideline NG128. London: NICE; 2019 (updated 2022).

guideline.name: JBDS-IP — The hospital management of hypoglycaemia in adults with diabetes mellitus
guideline.section: Hypoglycaemia <4.0 mmol/L; conscious and able to swallow: quick-acting carbohydrate, recheck in 10–15 min; unconscious, fitting or nil by mouth: IV glucose (10% or 20%) or IM glucagon; sulfonylurea-induced hypoglycaemia can be prolonged or recur — monitor and review the drug
guideline.citation: Joint British Diabetes Societies for Inpatient Care. The hospital management of hypoglycaemia in adults with diabetes mellitus (JBDS-IP 01, revised edition; year to be confirmed).

rationale: Hypoglycaemia is the classic treatable stroke mimic. NICE NG128 requires glucose to be excluded before stroke treatment; JBDS: IV glucose or glucagon.
